study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individual deviations from normative models of brain structure in a large cross-sectional schizophrenia cohort

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used data from the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB), a multi-site cohort collected across five sites in Australia (Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Newcastle). All sites used Siemens Avanto MRI scanners with the same acquisition sequence. After excluding participants with MRI artifacts, the sample comprised 517 individuals (322 schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder, 195 healthy controls).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Participants comprising the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank [28] with structural and diffusion-weighted MRI, genetic data, and symptom severity ratings were considered eligible." ... "Participants were recruited from five sites in Australia, with all sites implementing exactly the same recruitment procedures"

answer.ASRB (healthy controls, n=195): normative model training and validation (10-fold cross-validation: n=175 training, n=20 testing per fold)

answer.ASRB (schizophrenia, n=322): clinical application (individual deviation mapping from normative range)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy controls from the ASRB were used to establish normative ranges of variation in FA and CT via quantile regression, with 10-fold cross-validation (n=175 training, n=20 test per fold, repeated 20 times) to validate the normative model. Individuals with schizophrenia were then positioned on the normative percentile charts to determine individual deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "normative ranges of variation in FA and CT for each tract and region, respectively, were established based on the healthy comparison individuals (n = 195)" ... "percentile curves were fitted using a randomly selected subset of healthy individuals (n = 175, training set) and the proportion of remaining healthy individuals residing within the 5-95% percentiles (normative range) was enumerated (n = 20, test set). This was repeated for 20 randomly selected test-training subsets, using a tenfold cross-validation framework."

model-1.model-name: quantile regression normative model (FA and CT)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model framework (quantile regression) was applied to both FA (48 white matter tracts) and CT (68 cortical regions). The full healthy control sample (n=195) was used overall. In 10-fold cross-validation, n=175 were used for training and n=20 for testing per fold. The final model used all 195 healthy controls.
